approachQuestion.prompt:
Uniform Banner Edits

A lowercase banner string may have at most budget of its characters changed to any lowercase letter. Return the greatest length of a contiguous segment that can become a single repeated letter using that many changes. Changes outside the chosen segment are irrelevant.

Limits and assumptions:
• 0 ≤ n ≤ 200000; 0 ≤ budget ≤ n; alphabet is exactly a to z.
• Return only a length and do not modify banner. A change affects one position.

Examples:
1. banner = "abaca", budget = 1 → 3, by changing b in "aba" to a.
2. banner = "abcd", budget = 0 → 1.
3. banner = "", budget = 0 → 0.

Choose one approach.
constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 200000; 0 ≤ budget ≤ n; alphabet is exactly a to z.
Return only a length and do not modify banner. A change affects one position.

options.text: Maintain 26 letter counts in a moving segment. Recompute their greatest count after each change to a boundary. Shrink while segment length minus greatest count exceeds budget, and record the best valid length.
options.feedback: The least edits for a segment equal its length minus the most common letter count. Removing a prefix cannot increase that least edit count.

options.text: Binary-search a feasible length, testing every segment of that length with 26 rolling counts and the same edit formula.
options.feedback: Feasibility is monotone across lengths, so the result is correct, but repeated passes can be avoided by maintaining a variable segment.

options.text: Accept any segment with at most budget+1 distinct letters.
options.feedback: For "aabb" and budget=1 there are only two distinct letters, but making all four identical requires two changes.

options.text: Count adjacent unequal pairs and accept a segment whenever that count is at most budget.
options.feedback: For "aaabbb" and budget=1 there is one unequal neighboring pair, but converting the whole segment needs three changes.

feedback.reason: For any window, replacing all but its most frequent letter costs length-maxCount.
details: Keep 26 counts and recompute the maximum across all 26 after adding or removing a character. Extend right, shrink while length minus the current exact maximum exceeds budget, and update the best length after repair. Store no candidate strings.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only “Track the exact edit requirement” as specified in the method reveal. Choose the tightest worst-case running-time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Use unit-cost random access and arithmetic on machine words large enough for every index and sum.
Input is read-only and excluded from auxiliary space. The scalar or index-pair output is excluded; no candidate segment is copied.
The implementation is iterative with a constant call stack. No hashing is used; fixed alphabet arrays, when present, are direct indexed.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: A fixed 26-counter scan per boundary move keeps total work linear.
details: The edit formula is exact because retaining the most common letter minimizes changes. Deleting a character cannot increase the minimum changes required. Both boundaries move at most n times and each update scans exactly 26 counters, so time is O(n) and state is constant.
“O(n²) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Both boundaries advance at most n times, and scanning exactly 26 counters per move is constant in n.
“O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: The alphabet scan is fixed-size, not sorting; no sorted copy or candidate-string array is created.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: The only table has 26 counters regardless of banner length; all other state is scalar.
